This Mfa Is Filed Under Section 173(1) Of The

MOTOR ACCIDENT CLAIMS TRIBUNAL NO.4, SHAHAPUR AND ALLOW THE APPEAL TO GRANT THE COMPENSATION AMOUNT BY RS.12,65,402/- ONLY AS CLAIMED BY THE APPELLANT BEFORE THIS COURT AND ALSO ORDER FOR COSTS OF THIS APPEAL.

THIS APPEAL COMING ON FOR FURTHER ORDERS, THIS DAY, JUDGMENT WAS DELIVERED THEREIN AS UNDER:
CORAM: HON'BLE MRS JUSTICE P SREE SUDHA  ORAL JUDGMENT
This appeal is filed against the judgment and award dated 23.05.2023 passed by the Senior Civil Judge and JMFC and Additional MACT-4, Shahapur, in MVC No.31 of 2019.

2. The facts of the case are that, on 19.09.2018, while the claimant along with rider by name Ramu were NC: 2025:KHC-K:6488 HC-KAR returning from Shahapur to Shirwal village on motorcycle bearing registration No.KA-33-W-4840, the driver of the Auto bearing registration No.KA-33-A-7932 driven it in high speed and rash and negligent manner and dashed to the motorcycle of the claimant and thereby caused the accident, due to which, claimant sustained grievous injuries and fractures of right tibia and fibula.
3.
Therefore, he filed a claim petition before the Tribunal, claiming compensation of Rs.16,50,000/-.

The Tribunal, considering the entire evidence on record, granted compensation of Rs.3,84,598/-
Santoshkumar vs Shreekanta And Ors on 3 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/158953750/
2 with interest at 6% p.a.
from the date of petition till realisation and as it is a case of collision

,
respondent Nos.2 and 4 were directed to deposit the said amount in the ratio of 50:50 within one month.
4.

Aggrieved by the said judgment and award, the injured claimant has preferred this appeal, in which it is contended that, PW.2-Doctor has assessed the disability at 55% related to the right lower limb and 20% to the whole NC: 2025:KHC-K:6488 HC-KAR body, but the Tribunal has erroneously taken it as 6%; the amounts granted under other heads are meagre; the rate of interest is to be granted at 9% p.a. instead of 6% p.a.
Thus, requested for enhancement of the compensation.

5. Heard the arguments of both sides.
6.
As per Ex.P8 - Wound Certificate, the appellant sustained fracture of Tibia and Fibula.

PW.2 - Doctor stated that, there was shortening of right lower limb compared to the other limb and the claimant cannot run, squat and sit cross legged and finally assessed the disability at 55% to the right lower limb and 20% to whole body as per Ex.P9 - Disability Certificate.
But the Tribunal without any basis assessed the functional disability at 6% which is erroneous.
Hence, this Court finds it reasonable to re-assess the disability at 1/3 of 55% which comes to 18% to the whole body.

7. Though the appellant states his earning as Rs.10,000/- per month, the Tribunal has rightly assessed NC: 2025:KHC-K:6488 HC-KAR the notional income at Rs.11,750/- per month as per the guidelines stipulated by the Karnataka Sate Legal Services Authority for the accident of the year 2018.
Thus, the loss of future earnings would come to Rs.11,750 x 12 x 17 x 18% = Rs.4,31,460/- as against Rs.1,43,820/- awarded by the Tribunal.
8. The claimant was hospitalized for 6 days.

The Tribunal, considering the entire materials available on record has rightly awarded the compensation of Rs.50,000/- for pain and sufferings,
Rs.30,000/- for loss of amenities of life, Rs.25,000/- for attendant's charges, Rs.20,000/- for special food, Rs.65,528/- for medical expenses, Rs.35,250/- for loss of income during laid up period and Rs.15,000/- for loss of convenience, which do not call for any interference by this Court.
9. Accordingly, the compensation is enhanced from Rs.3,84,598/- to Rs.6,72,238/-.
There will be enhancement of Rs.2,87,640/- with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till realization.
NC: 2025:KHC-K:6488 HC-KAR 10.

In the result, the following order is passed:
 (i) Appeal is allowed in part.

(ii) The appellant/claimant is entitled for the Santoshkumar vs Shreekanta And Ors on 3 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/158953750/
3 enhanced compensation of Rs.2,87,640/- with interest at 6% per annum from the date of petition till the date of realisation.
(iii) Respondent Nos.2 and 4 - Insurance Companies are directed to deposit the aforesaid compensation amount along with interest in the ratio of 50:50, within one month from the date of this judgment.
(iv) On such deposit, the appellant is permitted to withdraw the entire amount along with interest accrued on it.
